tagline: Practical AI for real work. No coding, no hype.

tiles.label: Have someone build an AI automation for my business
tiles.headline: You picked: get an AI automation built for your business
tiles.intro: If the same admin task eats hours every week, a small custom AI workflow can usually take most of it away. You describe the problem; a specialist team scopes and builds it.
tips: Pick one repetitive task first: quotes, onboarding emails, document checks or reporting.
Write down how long it takes per week and who does it. That number decides whether a build is worth it.
Start with a small pilot, then extend. Avoid big-bang projects.

tiles.label: Payroll and HR admin take forever
tiles.headline: You picked: payroll and HR admin take forever
tiles.intro: For teams of roughly 1 to 50, most payroll pain comes from spreadsheets, re-keying and chasing paperwork. An all-in-one HR and payroll platform removes most of it.
tips: List every place staff data lives today. Each copy is a chance for errors.
Look for payroll, leave, onboarding and documents in one system.
Book a demo with your real pay run in mind and ask them to walk through it.

tiles.label: Too many HR, payroll and IT tools
tiles.headline: You picked: too many HR, payroll and IT tools
tiles.intro: Once a business passes about 15 staff, separate tools for payroll, devices, accounts and benefits start costing real hours. One connected platform can handle new starters end to end.
tips: Count the tools a new starter touches in week one.
Map who updates what when someone joins, moves or leaves.
Ask any vendor to demo a full starter-to-leaver journey.

tiles.label: I need a business bank account
tiles.headline: You picked: you need a business bank account
tiles.intro: Keeping business money separate makes bookkeeping, tax returns and invoicing far easier, even for sole traders.
tips: Check fees per transaction, not just the monthly price.
Look for invoicing and receipt capture built in.
Make sure it connects to your accounting software.

tiles.label: Cash flow is tight
tiles.headline: You picked: cash flow is tight
tiles.intro: Most cash-flow problems are timing problems: money is owed to you, but not yet paid. Fix the timing first, then look at funding.
tips: Send invoices the day work finishes and automate reminders.
Forecast the next 13 weeks of money in and out.
If you need funding, compare the total cost, not just the monthly payment.

tiles.label: I need an accountant
tiles.headline: You picked: you need an accountant
tiles.intro: A good online accountant handles your returns, bookkeeping and deadlines for a fixed monthly fee, so you are not chasing tax dates yourself.
tips: Ask exactly what the monthly fee includes: payroll, VAT, year-end.
Check they work with the accounting software you already use.
Get a named contact, not just a ticket queue.

tiles.label: Receipts and expenses are chaos
tiles.headline: You picked: receipts and expenses are chaos
tiles.intro: Shared company cards and paper receipts create hours of month-end reconciliation. Expense cards that capture receipts at the point of purchase remove most of it.
tips: Give each spender their own card with a set limit.
Capture the receipt photo at the moment of purchase.
Sync automatically to your accounting software.

tiles.label: Customers can't pay by card
tiles.headline: You picked: customers can't pay by card
tiles.intro: Trades, market stalls, cafes and salons lose sales and time chasing cash or bank transfers. A simple card reader or payment link fixes it.
tips: Compare the fee per transaction against your average sale.
Use payment links for jobs paid after the work is done.
Check how quickly money lands in your account.

tiles.label: I just need someone to do it
tiles.headline: You picked: you just need someone to do it
tiles.intro: Sometimes the right fix is a person, not software: a freelance bookkeeper, a virtual assistant or someone to set things up once.
tips: Write a one-page brief: the task, the hours, the outcome.
Start with a small paid trial task.
Keep logins in a password manager and share access, not passwords.

tiles.label: Not sure: show me where my time goes
tiles.headline: You picked: not sure yet
tiles.intro: That is the most common answer. Join the free list and get a short series that helps you find the admin tasks costing you the most hours, and what to fix first.
tips: For one week, jot down every admin task and how long it took.
Circle anything you do more than twice a week.
That circled list is where AI or better tools pay off first.
